summary: Steel eaten by flaking orange-brown rust in spreading patches, with bare grey metal showing between them.
_comment: Flaking rust on steel: bare mild steel on which iron oxide has grown in spreading patches, its crust cracked into flakes and some flakes fallen away. TwoLayer (MasterSet: two real layers, the mask choosing where layer 2 sits; the `rust -> TwoLayer` name exception, Phase71): layer 1 the bare steel (metallic, dulled, finely pitted), layer 2 the rust (a dielectric, rough), each a full generated set at the article's 0.1 m tile (tools/converters/base/gen_rust_onsteel.py), their mean colours Physically Based's Iron and Rust. Where the rust sits is the shared mask RustFlake01, sampled at its own 1 m, so the patches span cm to dm and never repeat at the article's tile; R is graded (0.5 the patch's edge), so layer_blend_balance grows or shrinks the rust, and layer_blend_contrast 0.6 crisps the flaky edge. maskset_blend MUST be non-zero (it defaults to 1 here) or the rust never shows. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): pitting (overlay 1, damage, gated in and round the rust), dust as a deposit (overlay 2, caught in the rust) and water spots (overlay 3, on the bare steel). Rebuilt in batch 261016-2 (the maintainer's redo): flaking rust, not the Phase71 test pattern's blocky speckle, seamless maps, its wear layers, and exactly 0.1 m (was 0.5 m under s01; Phase19 D-9).
name: Rust_OnSteel_Flaking_Base_s01_v01

sources.note: Layer 1, the bare steel: the generated map's mean colour is this, exactly; its roughness is not (a dulled, weathered face, see the judgement).
Layer 2, the rust: the generated map's mean colour is this, exactly, and the IOR; its roughness varies round 0.9 (see the judgement).

sources.why: Steel roughness about 0.55 for bare, weathered mild steel where the rust has flaked away (not polished); rust roughness about 0.9, a little below Physically Based's 1.0 so a lifted flake's edge keeps a faint sheen. layer_blend_contrast 0.6 so the rust's edge is crisp and flaky at the defaults; maskset_blend 1 so the rust shows fully.
